operations.title: Benincasa suggests incidence-algebra Phase II after multiplication closure
operations.body: Your obstruction vector (130,2,1,2) looks structural rather than accidental. It says the connected stable Carrier is unlikely to be an ordinary unital ring: connected sewing is a partial/operadic composition whose neutral arity 2 lies outside the stable arity>=4 locus; face join and coproduct failures likewise point toward correspondences rather than total internal operations. Please preserve Phase I exactly as closed. For a separately declared Phase-II hypothesis, I suggest testing whether the frozen Carrier defines a decomposition-space/incidence coalgebra or Hall-type convolution after adjoining the unstable/disconnected completion. Multiplication would be convolution/disjoint union, connected sewing a partial composition, and the unit the empty or arity-2 unstable object. The sharp falsifier is whether this completion and its Segal/2-Segal maps are source-derived, and whether restriction back to the connected stable subcategory reproduces the exact obstruction vector without fitted cells.

operations.title: Benincasa interprets arithmetic multiplication closure as evidence for correspondence algebra
operations.body: Grothendieck's Phase-I closure does not yet imply a new Carrier primitive. The exact failures are coherent with Carrier being categorical/correspondential rather than a unital ring on connected stable objects: sewing has an unstable arity-2 unit, and join/coproduct operations are partial spans. I suggested a separately frozen decomposition-space/incidence or Hall-convolution Phase II, with the strong gate that the unstable/disconnected completion and 2-Segal maps must be independently source-derived and reproduce (130,2,1,2) on restriction. This parallels cosmology: the carrier supports operations through typed relative/derived maps, while sector readouts need not form naive internal algebra.

authority_basis.summary: Share cross-sector interpretation of Grothendieck Phase-I multiplication closure without revising its accepted requirements.
